## Where wildlife is observed on a tour through Colombia and Peru

**Combining Peru and Colombia offers an introduction to several of South America's natural zones, but the itinerary must be examined day by day.** One tour focuses chiefly on historic cities surrounded by beautiful landscapes; another has dedicated nature excursions outside these two countries. No thematic label alone guarantees an encounter with any particular animal species.

Our wildlife catalog features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with these principal countries and the Wildlife and Safari theme. The relevant [32-day itinerary through eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) includes the Galápagos Islands in Ecuador. For comparison, [Peru & Colombia Discovery](/multi-country/tour/peru-colombia-discovery/) covers two countries over 14 days and focuses on culture and nature, without a stated wildlife-watching program. **Colombia + Peru is a selected intersection within the larger route here, not a standalone continuous section with its own dedicated nature program.**

If the overall routes and logistics are your priority, see [Colombia + Peru tours](/multi-country/colombia_peru/). Here we examine the nature experiences you can reasonably expect from the actual itineraries.

## Peru: mountain ecosystems and a high-altitude lake

In [Peru](/peru/), the journey first passes through [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), then climbs into the Andes toward [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). The archaeological complex is situated amid montane tropical forest on the eastern slopes of the Andes. Its natural setting is as remarkable as its Inca history: terraces and stone buildings are built into the steep terrain. However, visiting the monument on either of the two active tours does not mean there is a separate wildlife-observation program or a multi-day nature expedition.

The next natural contrast is the road across high passes to [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). The lake lies at roughly 3,810 meters above sea level, far higher than Lima's coast. The 14-day program includes visits to the Uros and Taquile islands. They offer opportunities to experience lake scenery and local life, but the main confirmed activities are sightseeing and learning about the culture of island communities. These days should not be advertised as a specialist birdwatching trip, a safari or a chance to see rare species.

For high-altitude travel, acclimatization, clothing that protects against wind and sun, and moderate exertion after flights are important. Even a short walk up steps in Cusco feels different from one at sea level. This matters more than trying to squeeze another nature attraction into an already full day.

## Colombia: a lagoon, the Andes and the Caribbean Sea

The Colombian section of the [14-day tour](/multi-country/tour/peru-colombia-discovery/) runs through [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), [Lake Guatavita](/colombia/place/lake-guatavita/), [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/) and [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/). For nature lovers, the most striking change is the transition from cool high-altitude landscapes to the tropical Caribbean coast.

[Guatavita](/colombia/place/lake-guatavita/) is a mountain lake known both for its natural surroundings and for the history of rituals that gave rise to the legend of El Dorado. A visit here combines culture and scenery; sightseeing at the lake is not a substitute for specialist wildlife observation.

In [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), the itinerary includes the Old Town, and a separate day may offer a trip to Barú Island. What the outing involves depends on the chosen option: the Caribbean coast, beaches and marine environment are not the same as organized scuba diving, a marine-biology excursion or guaranteed animal sightings. Before adding such an activity, compare its exact contents with the time remaining after transfers.

The Colombian section of the [32-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) is arranged differently: after arrival from Ecuador, it covers Medellín, Guatapé, Cartagena, Bogotá and Zipaquirá. These are primarily cities, historical experiences and landscape excursions. It would be incorrect to suggest that every day in Colombia is dedicated to wildlife watching.

## Where the genuine wildlife-watching takes place on the grand tour

The clearest nature-and-wildlife emphasis on the 32-day itinerary is in **the Galápagos Islands of Ecuador**, outside the Colombia + Peru pair. The route includes Santa Cruz Island and a separate boat excursion, with one of two alternatives: North Seymour with Bachas Beach **or** South Plaza with Carrion Point. Both options are not visited together. This is the section that offers opportunities to encounter island birds and the archipelago's distinctive wildlife; particular sightings remain unpredictable natural events, not guarantees.

| Itinerary | Nature focus |
|---|---|
| [Peru + Colombia, 14 days](/multi-country/tour/peru-colombia-discovery/) | Andes, Titicaca, Guatavita, Caribbean |
| [Eight countries, 32 days](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) | The same countries plus the Galápagos in Ecuador |

The table below compares programs that include watching wild animals or birds. Scenic routes without such observations can be compared in the [nature-travel selection](/multi-country/colombia_peru/interests/nature/). On a multi-country tour, wildlife encounters may be scheduled outside the countries named in the selection's title: check the entire route and specific days.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

This distinction changes the choice. A focused journey is suitable for discovering mountain lakes, landscapes and the natural surroundings of historical monuments. If your aim is to spend specific days on islands watching wildlife, compare the longer route and [other multi-country wildlife-watching tours](/multi-country/interests/wildlife/) by their actual stops.

## What to consider when planning a nature-focused journey

**Choose what you want to observe before choosing the geography.** Peru's highlands, Colombia's lakes, Caribbean beaches and the wildlife of the Galápagos offer different conditions and experiences. A catalog theme alone cannot answer the question, 'Which animals will I see in Peru and Colombia?'

Four things matter in practice. First, altitude: flying from Lima to Cusco and traveling to Titicaca mean a major change in conditions. Second, duration: an organized nature excursion needs dedicated time, not a few spare hours between flights. Third, the season and weather in each region; the Andean plateau and Caribbean lowlands do not share a single 'best month.' Finally, access rules for natural areas, particularly islands and protected sites, must be factored into the particular tour.

We help match the itinerary to travelers' interests and coordinate the sequence of stops and flights. Specialist wildlife-watching trips, additional guides or boat excursions count as included only if explicitly listed in the conditions of the selected product. For a more focused search, explore [wildlife-watching tours through Peru](/interests/wildlife/tours/peru/) and [wildlife-watching tours through Colombia](/interests/wildlife/tours/colombia/): compare their daily activities, not just the number of destinations.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Peru and Colombia

### Can I expect to see wildlife in both countries?

Only if the relevant excursions are explicitly included in the selected program. The tours discussed here include mountain lakes, natural scenery and coastal stops, but no separate guaranteed wildlife-watching in both countries.

### Why is an eight-country tour included in this selection?

Because Peru and Colombia are among its principal countries, while the additional Wildlife and Safari theme applies to the whole journey. Scheduled wildlife experiences take place on Santa Cruz and on one of the two Galápagos island excursions in Ecuador.

### How does Titicaca differ from Guatavita?

[Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) is a vast high-altitude lake with island communities included in the Peruvian itinerary. [Guatavita](/colombia/place/lake-guatavita/) is a mountain lake visited in Colombia for its natural setting and the El Dorado legend. The excursions differ in both what they cover and how they are reached.

### Is specialist trekking experience necessary?

The sightseeing programs described do not list experience in demanding trekking as a requirement. However, high-altitude exertion and long transfers call for appropriate physical preparation; individual limitations are best discussed with a doctor before traveling.

## Colombia, Peru and Uruguay: which itinerary is actually offered?

The combination of [Colombia](/colombia/), [Peru](/peru/) and [Uruguay](/uruguay/) is appealing for its diversity. In Montevideo you explore the history of the Río de la Plata, in Peru you visit Lake Titicaca, Cusco and Machu Picchu, and in Colombia you discover Medellín, Cartagena and Bogotá.

Our selection currently features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The relevant [32-day Eight Countries of South America tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) passes through all three countries, **but also includes Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Bolivia and Ecuador**. The Atacama and the Bolivian highlands lie between the Uruguay and Peru sections; Quito and the Galápagos Islands come between Peru and Colombia. The selection's title does not mean there is a separate three-country itinerary without those stops.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

{{#if catalog.hasComparableUsdPrice}}
The lowest comparable program price in this selection is {{catalog.minUsdPriceLabel}}. Accommodation arrangements, domestic flights, meals and exclusions are specified in the description of the individual tour.
{{/if}}

Traveling only through Colombia, Peru and Uruguay would require recalculating the route and tickets: covering the southern part of the continent, the Andes and then Colombia's cities is generally easier with major flights than by trying to piece together a route from neighboring overland legs.

## What you will see in each country

| Country | Actual section of the tour |
|---|---|
| Uruguay | A day in Montevideo from Buenos Aires |
| Peru | Titicaca, Cusco, Machu Picchu and Lima |
| Colombia | Medellín, Cartagena, Bogotá and Zipaquirá |

**Uruguay.** On day nine, the itinerary includes an excursion to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) with a return to Buenos Aires. In the capital's center, you can see Independence Square and historic neighborhoods. The time available depends on the ferry timetable, border procedures and return departure. It is primarily a city day, so distant excursions elsewhere in the country cannot be combined with it without changing the program.

**Peru.** After La Paz in Bolivia, the route passes through Tiwanaku and the border toward [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). A tourist bus then crosses the Andes to Cusco, followed by a separate day at [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), sightseeing at Inca monuments and a flight to Lima. The Peruvian section includes both high-altitude transfers and a major city on the Pacific coast.

**Colombia.** Toward the end of the journey, travelers visit [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), El Peñol and Guatapé, Comuna 13, then Cartagena, [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) and Zipaquirá's Salt Cathedral. The Colombian section cannot be reduced to a single 'tropical holiday': Bogotá is high in the Andes, Cartagena is on the hot coast, and Medellín lies in a mountain valley.

## Altitude in Peru: preparing for the demanding part of the journey

The main physical challenge of this combination is not the long walks in Montevideo or Cartagena but the **Bolivia–Titicaca–Cusco** section. The current itinerary includes days at high-altitude lagoons and Uyuni before entering Peru, followed by La Paz. Travelers then reach Titicaca and continue to Cusco, with the bus crossing the high La Raya Pass.

Even someone in good physical shape can develop altitude sickness after a rapid ascent. Sensible acclimatization, enough rest, moderate exertion during the first high-altitude days and a prior discussion of medical contraindications with a doctor are helpful. This is especially important for travelers with cardiovascular or lung conditions. Medical decisions and preventive medication must be determined individually, not from a travel article.

**Machu Picchu requires its own arrangements.** Entry tickets are tied to specific circuits and admission times; Peru's government opened ticket sales for 2026 in advance. The excursion day depends on an available entry slot, the train and transfers between Cusco and Machu Picchu. Do not buy just any flight and assume that tickets for a preferred date and convenient connections will then be available.

If Andean heritage and Machu Picchu are your main priorities, compare [Peru tours](/peru/tour/) with the extended continent-wide itinerary: shorter programs may distribute acclimatization and sightseeing days differently.

## Logistics: why this is not a chain of three neighboring countries

The sequence of the current 32-day journey is **Montevideo – return to Argentina – Chile – Bolivia – Peru – Ecuador – Colombia**. The journey from Lima to Colombia must not be shown as a direct flight: Quito, the Galápagos and Guayaquil are scheduled between them.

Planning involves several separate operations. First, confirm the Buenos Aires–Montevideo–Buenos Aires ferry trip. Next, coordinate the Andean sections, taking altitude and transport stops into account. After Peru come the mainland flight into Ecuador, the island program with its own access rules, and then the flight to Medellín and domestic travel within Colombia.

We help coordinate the stages, allow reasonable connection times and align transfers with hotel stays. Changing the route means recalculating both transport and sightseeing days. Cutting the time buffer between Machu Picchu and a flight departing from another part of the country is especially risky: a train or road delay could disrupt the next stages.

## Entry requirements and money on each part of the journey

For a traveler with a **Russian international passport**, entry conditions must be checked for all eight countries actually visited, not just three. This includes visa rules, passport validity, return tickets and transit requirements. Particular attention is needed for the return from Uruguay to Argentina: it is a second crossing of the Argentine border, even if the Montevideo excursion lasts only one day.

Colombia provides a free advance travel-information service called Check-Mig. The migration authority describes it as recommended rather than mandatory for every tourist. Peru's Machu Picchu permits and Ecuador's island TCT card concern **entry to particular sites and territories**; they do not replace border documents.

Peru uses the **sol**, Colombia the **Colombian peso**, and Uruguay the **Uruguayan peso**. The currency used to pay for the tour itself should be distinguished from money for incidental expenses. Exchange rates at airports and in cities, cash-withdrawal fees and card acceptance may differ. Whether a Russian-issued bank card can be used abroad must be confirmed with the particular issuer; the whole payment plan should not depend on one method. US dollars can be useful as a reserve, but no one guarantees they will be accepted everywhere.

## Weather and luggage: three sets of conditions

Spring arrives in the Southern Hemisphere when the itinerary reaches Montevideo in late October. Peru's Andes bring much sharper differences between daytime and nighttime temperatures; mornings near Titicaca or on high mountain passes can be cold even when the sun shines during the day. Cartagena in Colombia is generally warm and humid, while Bogotá's weather reflects its mountainous elevation.

The packing challenge is to combine **a windproof jacket, warm mid-layer, sturdy footwear and lightweight tropical clothing** without excessive weight. There are many domestic flights on the route, so baggage allowances should be checked for every carrier, including flights in Ecuador and Colombia. Keep documents, essential medication and a change of clothes in hand luggage, while observing airline restrictions.

On a long journey, it is also worth discussing travel insurance: it should cover the planned altitudes and types of activity, not merely the country names. Medical advice and any vaccination requirements should be checked for the actual regions visited.

## What to choose instead of the 32-day itinerary

If you want **Machu Picchu and Colombia's cities**, but Montevideo is a secondary priority, a different arrangement of flights and days may make more sense. If you want to see **both Uruguay and northern South America**, you will need to accept considerable distances or allow more time. The 32-day tour addresses this through a broad itinerary in which the geography between the three selected countries is itself an important part of the experience.

To compare more focused routes, browse the [Colombia tour catalog](/colombia/tour/) and [Uruguay tour selection](/uruguay/tour/). Their programs should not automatically be treated as shortened versions of this eight-country tour: check the exact contents on the individual tour pages.

## Frequently asked questions about travel in Colombia, Peru and Uruguay

### Can I fly straight from Montevideo to Peru?

That is an option to consider for a new custom itinerary, but **it is not part of the current tour**. After Montevideo, the journey returns to Buenos Aires and continues through Chile and Bolivia. Recalculating flights would change both the price and the program.

### Is this journey suitable for people who do not tolerate altitude well?

The eight-country tour includes high-altitude sections in Bolivia and Peru. Before booking, review the itinerary with a doctor and discuss a gentler alternative with Ada Tours if necessary. Simply reducing walking excursions does not eliminate the altitude of overnight stays and transfers.

### Can I visit Machu Picchu without an advance ticket?

Relying on that is risky: access depends on a ticket for a specific circuit and admission time. For dates in 2026, Peru's government arranges advance ticket sales, so train times and entry slots should be planned together.

### How much time is allocated to Uruguay?

On the tour described, it is a one-day excursion from Buenos Aires to Montevideo, returning to Argentina. Other Uruguayan cities or an overnight stay would require additional days.

### Which part of the trip is most demanding logistically?

First come the long Andean transfers and the Machu Picchu visit; then the route from Peru through Ecuador and the Galápagos to Colombia. Allow enough time for transport, island procedures and connections.

## Peru: altitude matters more than athletic difficulty

The Peruvian section begins near [Lake Titicaca and Puno](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). The program includes a trip to the Uros Islands, followed by a bus journey to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) with stops in Andean settlements and at La Raya Pass. The pass is approximately 4,400 meters above sea level. That is a significant altitude even for someone traveling by bus.

The next day is devoted to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/): a full-day excursion from Cusco with a return by train. **This tour does not include a multi-day hike along the Inca Trail.** If trekking is what you want, an itinerary change must be arranged separately; an adventure label in the catalog does not mean the hike is included.

Here, physical preparation is primarily about coping with altitude, walking around historic sites and keeping up with a busy schedule. If you have cardiovascular or respiratory limitations, discuss high-altitude travel with a doctor before booking. Clothing for cool mornings and sun protection are both useful: weather in Puno and Cusco differs from that of coastal Lima.

## Colombia: busy sightseeing days and long transfers

After Ecuador, the tour reaches [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/). From here, an eight-hour outing is scheduled to [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) and El Peñón rock. The excursion includes the town, reservoir and rock formation, but climbing the steps to the summit is not confirmed as an included service. Whether to make that climb should be decided separately, taking personal fitness and available time into account.

Next come sightseeing in Medellín and Comuna 13, a flight to [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), and then [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) with its historic center, museums and Monserrate. A separate day is devoted to Zipaquirá. The trip provides opportunities to see mountain regions and architecture, but the Colombian days do not include a confirmed program of rafting, mountain biking or demanding trekking.

When packing, consider the transition from hot Cartagena to cooler, high-altitude Bogotá. On busy city days, comfortable shoes and opportunities to take a break are more useful than specialist hiking equipment.

## Uruguay: one sightseeing day between other countries

The trip to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) departs from Buenos Aires: an early transfer to the port, a ferry crossing, a city tour with an English-speaking guide, free time and a return ferry to Argentina. Planned sights include [Independence Square](/uruguay/place/montevideo-independence-square/), the [Old Town](/uruguay/place/montevideo-old-town/) and the [Cathedral](/uruguay/place/montevideo-cathedral/). Ferry tickets are included in this tour.

It is a full one-day city excursion, **without a sporting or wilderness adventure in Uruguay**. It adds another country to the long itinerary but does not replace a proper coastal trek in Uruguay. The day's main considerations are the ferry timetable and two sets of border formalities, with a return to Argentina. Travel documents must permit re-entry into the departure country.

## Preparing documents, payments and baggage

For Russian citizens holding a valid ordinary international passport, according to official information checked on **October 16, 2026**, Colombia, Peru and Uruguay allow visa-free tourist trips of up to 90 days within the applicable 180-day periods. However, this route covers eight countries, and travelers must re-enter Argentina after visiting Montevideo. Before buying tickets, check every border crossing, permitted length of stay, flight connection conditions and passport validity for the traveler's particular citizenship.

Different currencies are used: the Colombian peso, the Peruvian sol and the Uruguayan peso. US dollars may serve as a reserve for exchange, but payment in USD cannot be assumed everywhere. Check whether your specific bank card will work, especially if it was issued in Russia, before departure; plan cash, fees and a safe exchange method separately.

For the high-altitude bus transfer and the ferry day, bring a small carry-on bag with medication, documents, a warm layer and rain protection. Baggage allowances may vary between airlines on the itinerary; check the conditions of each domestic flight against the ticket. Ada Tours helps coordinate the sequence, connection buffers and transport, while the exact included services are defined by the selected program.

If you want a more technical adventure, explore [multi-country adventure tours](/multi-country/interests/adventure/) and [adventure trips in Peru](/interests/adventure/tours/peru/): compare the format and activities of individual itineraries.

## Frequently asked questions about adventures in Colombia, Peru and Uruguay

### Is the trek to Machu Picchu included?

No. The program describes a one-day excursion from Cusco with a return train journey; a separate multi-day trek would have to be arranged separately.

### Do I need to be an athlete for the Uruguay day?

No sporting activities are scheduled. Being prepared for an early departure, the ferry crossing, a city walk and the return to Buenos Aires matters more.

### Where is the greatest altitude exposure?

In Peru, it involves transfers through the Andes, Puno and Cusco. The complete 32-day itinerary also has its most demanding high-altitude road sections in Bolivia. These conditions matter even for travelers without sporting plans.

### Can the itinerary be shortened to these three countries?

This would require a different sequence of flights and crossings. Our selection includes one grand tour covering eight countries, so a standalone three-country price or duration cannot be inferred automatically.

The defining contrast is that Peru reveals the archaeology and culture of the Andes, Colombia combines colonial architecture with modern urban history, and Uruguay adds a day of discovery in the capital on the other side of the Río de la Plata.

## Peru: from Lake Titicaca to the Inca capital

The Peruvian itinerary begins at [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). A visit to the Uros Islands introduces travelers to community life and the traditional use of reeds. A tourist bus then travels toward [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) via Andahuaylillas, Raqchi, Sicuani, La Raya Pass and Pucará. The road is part of the cultural route rather than an empty transfer: the stops introduce pre-Inca and Inca history.

A separate day is devoted to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). It includes a guided excursion in English and a return to Cusco by train. The following day covers Qorikancha, Qenqo, Puka Pukara, Tambomachay and Sacsayhuamán with a Russian-speaking guide. This sequence enables comparisons between monuments but leaves little free time for additional museums in Cusco.

In [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), the itinerary shifts to a different period: Miraflores, the historic center, Plaza Mayor and the Santo Domingo monastery. The Cathedral may be replaced with the MALI museum if it is closed. This is a practical reason to agree on opening days, tickets and any substitution of one museum for another ahead of time. Necessary domestic flights and sightseeing schedules are taken from the specific tour program.

## Colombia: three cities, three different histories

In [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), a city tour, including Comuna 13, is scheduled after the visit to Guatapé. It tells the story of changes to the urban environment and public spaces. Next comes [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), with its historic center, San Felipe de Barajas Fortress, city gates and the old architecture of the Caribbean coast.

In [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), the itinerary includes historic La Candelaria, the Gold Museum, the Casa de Moneda, the Botero Collection and an overview of Plaza Bolívar, followed by Monserrate. Museum visits depend on the day of the week: the Gold Museum is generally closed on Mondays, while the Casa de Moneda and Botero Collection are generally closed on Tuesdays. **Actual opening hours for the planned day must be checked before traveling**; a museum visit should not be promised without considering the calendar.

A separate excursion to [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/) focuses on the Salt Cathedral. The Colombian section differs from the Peruvian one: it has fewer Inca monuments and more urban heritage from different periods, religious architecture and art collections.

## Uruguay: historic Montevideo in one day

[Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) is visited by ferry from Buenos Aires. With an English-speaking guide, travelers explore [Independence Square](/uruguay/place/montevideo-independence-square/), the [Old Town](/uruguay/place/montevideo-old-town/), the [Cathedral](/uruguay/place/montevideo-cathedral/) and the port area of the capital. Free time follows before the return ferry to Argentina.

It is a convenient introduction for a first visit, but **one day is not enough to explore Uruguay's history in depth** or travel to colonial towns beyond Montevideo. Including such places would require overnight stays and a revised itinerary. On the existing tour, time needed for the ferry and border formalities should not be sacrificed for additional museum visits.

## Organizing visits without wasting time

On a route with several culturally rich cities, the main constraints are site opening calendars, altitude and flights. In Peru, the bus journey from Puno to Cusco crosses high-altitude areas; fatigue after the journey should be considered rather than overloading the evening. In Colombia, transfers from Medellín to Cartagena and then from Cartagena to Bogotá are by air, and museum plans depend on the day of the week. The Uruguay excursion is tied to early outgoing and return ferries.

For Russian citizens holding an ordinary international passport, official information as of **October 16, 2026** allows visa-free tourist entry to Peru, Colombia and Uruguay for up to 90 days within the specified 180-day periods. However, the full 32-day itinerary covers eight countries, including **re-entry into Argentina** after Montevideo. ### Can I visit Machu Picchu and Cusco without a separate trek?

One day of sightseeing, with ferries to and from Buenos Aires. A more in-depth visit to Uruguay would require changing the itinerary.

### What if a museum in Bogotá is closed?

Check each museum's calendar in advance and agree on the day's sequence. One site's closure does not make the rest of Bogotá's attractions unavailable.

A different route can be discussed, but it would be an independent project with new flights, dates and conditions. The program offered here covers eight countries.

## Nature in Colombia, Peru and Uruguay: how the three sections differ

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. [Colombia](/colombia/), [Peru](/peru/) and [Uruguay](/uruguay/) are part of a [32-day journey through eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), but each offers something quite different. Of these three countries, the most extensive nature-focused experiences are in Peru's highlands; Colombia has a standout day at a rock formation and reservoir, while Uruguay is represented by sightseeing in Montevideo.

The defining feature of this combination is the change in landscape: the broad expanse of water on the Altiplano, mountain passes and steep green slopes around Inca monuments, followed by rolling hills and the winding shoreline of the Guatapé reservoir. The Uruguayan section is better suited to discovering a riverside city than to a dedicated nature hike.

## Peru: high-altitude waters and mountain valleys

Entering Peru from Bolivia, travelers stop in the [Puno and Lake Titicaca area](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) for an excursion to the reed islands of Uros. Nature and culture are closely connected here: local people live on a high-altitude lake, while the views across the water and open plateau are very different from familiar tropical coastlines.

Travelers then take a special tourist bus across [La Raya Pass](/peru/place/la-raya-pass/) toward [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/). The itinerary combines mountain views with stops at historical sites, lunch in Sicuani and an evening arrival in the city. It is a full day in the Andes, but no multi-day trek is scheduled. Ascents and temperature variations should be considered in advance, particularly after the high-altitude sections in Bolivia.

[Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) adds another landscape to the journey: the ancient city stands on a steep mountain ridge, surrounded by a transition zone between the high Andes and the upper Amazon basin. The program includes a guided tour in English, lunch and a return to Cusco by train. Travelers come to see a historical monument **in its natural setting**, rather than undertake a separate hike along Inca trails.

After Cusco come Lima and the flight to Ecuador. If you are particularly interested in Peru's nature, explore the [country's nature-tour catalog](/interests/nature/tours/peru/).

## Colombia: a day among reservoirs and several cities

The Colombian section begins in [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/). Its strongest nature-focused episode is a visit to [El Peñón de Guatapé](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/), [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) and the Peñol–Guatapé reservoir. The focus is on a rocky massif, green hills, islands and water views; the excursion day lasts eight hours.

This is not the same landscape as Titicaca: instead of an open high-altitude plateau, travelers see an intricate reservoir surrounded by lower, green slopes. The contrast is especially striking when comparing photos and memories of the journey, but **the program does not contain a separate conservation expedition in Colombia**.

The route then continues through Comuna 13, Cartagena, Bogotá and Zipaquirá. Bogotá is situated in the Andes, and Monserrate offers sweeping views of the city and mountains, but these days are primarily cultural sightseeing. For a trip focused more closely on Colombia's natural attractions, see the [themed tour selection](/interests/nature/tours/colombia/).

## Uruguay: the Río de la Plata waterfront without a scheduled wildlife safari

On day nine of the grand journey, the group leaves Buenos Aires by ferry across the Río de la Plata for [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/). The city tour includes the port, Independence Square, historic neighborhoods and the cathedral. The guide speaks English, and there is free time after sightseeing before the return ferry. **There is no overnight stay in Uruguay.**

The river crossing offers a view of the broad expanse of water and the urban shoreline, but the day is devoted to discovering the capital. [Uruguay](/uruguay/) has other natural regions and beaches; they are not included stops on this tour. If nature is your main reason for traveling, treat the Uruguayan day as a complement, not an equal substitute for Peru's mountain excursions.

## Why this is not a ready-made Montevideo–Cusco–Medellín route

This selection highlights countries on the complete itinerary, but it does not imply direct transfers between those three places. In the actual sequence, Uruguay comes first, with a return to Argentina, followed by Chile and Bolivia; only then do travelers reach Peru. The Ecuadorian section, including the Galápagos Islands, lies between Peru and Colombia. The journey covers eight countries in all, and removing intermediate days changes the entire calculation for flights and accommodation.

| Section | What is included |
|---|---|
| Uruguay | Montevideo and a return by ferry |
| Peru | Titicaca, the road through the Andes, Machu Picchu |
| Colombia | El Peñón, Guatapé and city panoramas |

When planning this route, consider how you cope with altitude in Peru, the duration of the group bus day, temperature changes between night and morning, and time spent flying. In Uruguay, the excursion is tied to the ferry timetable; in Colombia, transfers alternate with city tours. One uniform set of clothing will not suffice for all 32 days: layers, shoes suitable for city walks and uneven paths, and protection from sun and wind are practical choices.

If you want to visit only these three countries, transport logistics and current travel conditions must be planned separately. ### Are there many nature excursions in Uruguay on this tour?

### Can I add a multi-day trek in Peru without changing the tour?

The current itinerary includes a Machu Picchu sightseeing trip with a return by train. A multi-day hike would require changes to the days, transport and conditions.

### Why does Uruguay appear in a nature selection for Colombia and Peru?

The selection algorithm shows tours whose principal countries include all three destinations and which have the Nature theme. The actual nature itinerary must be checked day by day: Uruguay is visited for Montevideo on this trip, while the strongest nature sections are in other countries.

### Does the eight-country tour include natural attractions beyond these three countries?

Yes. The complete itinerary includes, for example, the Atacama, Bolivia's lagoons, Uyuni and the Galápagos Islands. They are part of the journey even though they do not appear in the name of this three-country filter.
